note: Guyana: by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation's own list of the countries whose nationals don't need a visa (updated 17 July 2025), CARICOM's members (6 months, from Wikipedia's copy) and the British Virgin Islands, and the others listed, for the stays shown (90 days where the list gives them, as for Panama, Costa Rica and the Dominican Republic, 30 for Qatar, the Maldives, Singapore, South Korea and South Africa; for Europe, North America, Japan and others the list gives no length, and Wikipedia's copy's 90 days are kept); everyone else needs a visa. Read on 2026-11-03: the list presents itself as the whole list, so the countries it leaves out, or exempts only for diplomatic or official passports, need a visa; it corrected Wikipedia's copy, read before, on Panama (90 days, not 180), Costa Rica and the Dominican Republic (90, not 30), Qatar (30, not 90), and on Cuba, Spain, Uruguay, Kuwait, Germany, Malaysia, Eswatini, Lesotho, the Cayman Islands and the Turks and Caicos Islands, which now need a visa (Germany's left out of a list that names its neighbours, so it is recorded here for the lead to confirm).
